I'd run the documented check before calling this done. The README says `make check` is the project's test command, and it runs the whole suite with `--golden`. Without that flag about half the tests are skipped, so the 6 passing tests in `tests/test_format.py` don't tell us whether rounding broke anything that uses the recorded station tables. It's read-only and short, so it won't cost you much of the ten minutes.

**File changes:** none before the run. `tides/format.py` is already edited.

**Command:**

<command>make check</command>

I'd then read the output for pytest failures, any skips, and ruff findings. I would not change tests or loosen assertions to get it green. If a golden test fails because its recorded values were unrounded, I'd stop and ask you before touching it, since that decides whether the recording or the code is right.

**Message to partner (sent after the run, with the real results filled in):**

> Rounding to 0.01 m is in `tides/format.py`, and `tests/test_format.py` passes (6 passed). That file alone doesn't cover the golden station tables, though, so I ran the README's `make check` (full pytest with `--golden`, then `ruff check .`) before calling it done.
>
> Result: `<pass/fail counts, any failing test names, any skips, ruff output>`.
>
> - If all green: it's safe to deploy from my side.
> - If anything is red: I've listed the failing tests by name above and haven't edited them. I'll tell you whether each one looks caused by my change (for example, golden values recorded before rounding) or was already failing, and you can decide whether to deploy.
>
